meta.title: School Route Atlas
meta.subtitle: Understand the courses. Know the exams. Keep university options open.
meta.scope: Public-school planning facts for Alberta and nine university routes. No personal student records, grades, registrations or completed-task claims.
meta.date_warning: Rules were checked in October 2026. Future offerings, fees, exam sessions and admission deadlines must be checked for the actual entry year.
meta.privacy: This guide does not connect to Moodle, myPass or a student's school records. Official links may require a private sign-in.
meta.limits: A calculated route is not permission to register, an approved graduation date or an admission guarantee. Learning topics are orientation summaries, not a substitute for the enrolled course outline.

labels.required: Required for the diploma or enrolled course
labels.goal: Needed for a particular university or route

overview.headline: Move faster without closing doors.
overview.summary: Finish the required courses, keep the marks needed for the next course, and choose university requirements before filling the remaining credits. Build alongside school rather than waiting for a particular campus.
overview.recommendation: Use Waterloo and Toronto as selective Canadian CS possibilities, Stanford as an ambitious application and Berkeley only after checking its subject mapping and cost. Calgary, Alberta, UBC, Santa Clara and San Jose State add different routes, not guaranteed backup offers.
key_points: Credits measure the amount of completed coursework. Marks measure performance. A five-credit course still awards five credits at 70% or 95%.
10, 20 and 30 are course levels, usually associated with Grades 10, 11 and 12. They are not the number of credits.
Alberta graduation, VVS registration and university admission have different requirements.
A course can earn credit at 50% while the next VVS course requires a higher final mark.
Not every 30-level course has a diploma exam. Math 31 has a school final but no diploma exam.
English 30-1 at VVS has both diploma parts but no separate school final. Its course-specific catalogue overrides an overbroad general exams page.
The selected route contains 22 courses for 102 credits. Selection is not VVS registration approval.
Science 30 can follow Physics 20 or Chemistry 20 at 65%; Science 20 is not needed in this selected route. Science 10 remains for Physics 20 and Chemistry 20 entry.
COM1255 is mandatory if not previously completed, counted once, with term placement confirmed by VVS.
start_here: Read the credit map to separate graduation minimums from university courses.
Open a course to see topics, prerequisites and actual assessments.
Open an exam to see where it happens and how access works.
Compare universities before treating the conditional timeline as your final program.

graduation.credit_explanation: You need at least 100 awarded high-school credits and the specified subject categories. Grade 9 studies and PATs do not themselves add these high-school credits.
graduation.passing_explanation: For a normal non-diploma course, credit usually requires a passing final mark. In a diploma-exam course, the normal official final mark blends 70% school mark with 30% diploma mark. Provincial exceptions can change this for a particular session.

requirements.name: English at 30 level
requirements.route_choice: Selected: English 10-1, 20-1 and 30-1, 15 credits. No -2 courses are selected.

requirements.name: Social Studies at 30 level
requirements.route_choice: Selected: Social Studies 10-1, 20-1 and 30-1, 15 credits. No -2 courses are selected.

requirements.name: Math at 20 level
requirements.route_choice: For the checked Waterloo CS route, continue through Math 30-1 and Math 31.

requirements.name: Science at 20 level
requirements.requirement: Science 20 or 24, Biology 20, Chemistry 20 or Physics 20. An approved Science 14 plus Science 10 combination can also meet the science minimum.
requirements.route_choice: Physics 20 and Chemistry 20 meet this category. Selected science courses also include Science 10 and 30, Physics 30 and Chemistry 30. Science 20 is not selected.

requirements.name: Physical Education 10
requirements.requirement: At least 3 credits, subject to an approved exemption
requirements.route_choice: The illustrated route uses the three-credit version.

requirements.name: Career and Life Management
requirements.requirement: 3 credits, subject to an approved exemption
requirements.route_choice: CALM is a course, not a provincial entrance exam.

requirements.name: An approved options group
requirements.requirement: 10 credits from approved categories such as CTS, fine arts, second languages or PE 20/30
requirements.route_choice: French 10-3Y, 20-3Y and 30-3Y provide 15 selected language credits. COM1255 adds one distinct credit. No Art or unnamed CTS groups are selected.

requirements.name: Additional senior credits
requirements.requirement: 10 credits in 30-level courses beyond the required English and Social Studies 30 courses
requirements.route_choice: Math 30-1 and Physics 30 alone provide 10. Math 31, Chemistry 30, Science 30 and French 30-3Y add selected senior credits.

graduation.bucket_warning: The selected courses total 102 credits, counted once each. Alberta still requires at least 100 and the subject categories. The 10 option credits and 10 additional senior credits are included within the same total, not added again. COM1255 counts once, including an existing award if previously completed.
warnings: 102 planned credits give only a two-credit margin above the 100-credit minimum; actual awards and category requirements still matter.
COM1255 is mandatory if not previously completed. Its one credit must not be counted twice.
No Biology, Science 20, accounting, Art 10 or unnamed CTS groups are selected. English and Social Studies stay on the -1 route.
Math 31 and English 30-1 are goal-specific choices, not the only ways to meet Alberta graduation minimums.

courses.name: English Language Arts 10-1
courses.subject: English
courses.purpose: Build the academic English route toward university entry and English 30-1.
learn: Read short stories, poetry, nonfiction, drama, a novel and film.
Explain a text's meaning with specific supporting details.
Plan, revise and control your own writing.

prerequisites.note: The catalogue also permits English 10-2 at 70%. Grade 9 final report and registration requirements still apply.

courses.assessment: Five units with assignments and quizzes, including remotely supervised assessments. No diploma exam. The catalogue does not provide a complete final-exam count.
access_steps: After approved registration, open the course introduction in Moodle.
Read its timeline, supervised-assessment rules and required novel/film choices.
Use the teacher's release conditions for each assessment.
study_steps: Read the required text yourself.
Make your own short evidence notes.
Practise a paragraph with a clear claim and a relevant example.
warnings: The catalogue expects at least 8-10 hours per week and adherence to its timeline.
AI tools are prohibited in any capacity in this course, including Grammarly. Do not use this guide as permission for AI help with course work.

courses.name: English Language Arts 20-1
courses.subject: English
courses.purpose: Develop the reading and writing needed for English 30-1.
learn: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, viewing and representing.
Authorial choices and context.
Personal, critical and creative responses to print and multimedia texts.

prerequisites.note: English 20-2 at 70% is another catalogue entry route.

courses.assessment: Most assessments are proctored. Follow the enrolled course outline for the complete assessment list. No provincial diploma exam.
access_steps: Read the Moodle introduction and teacher timeline.
Obtain the exact physical texts the course names.
Prepare valid photo ID, external and built-in cameras, and microphone as the catalogue requires.
study_steps: Annotate the actual required texts yourself.
Connect a choice of language or structure to its effect.
Practise a clear response under the course's permitted conditions.
warnings: The course bans AI in any capacity, including Grammarly and Quillbot.
Text substitutions are not permitted. Follow the exact materials list.

courses.name: English Language Arts 30-1
courses.subject: English
courses.purpose: Meet the checked CS admission English requirement and the diploma English category.
learn: Poetry, visuals, short stories, nonfiction, Shakespeare, film and a novel.
Personal and critical responses supported by text knowledge.
Reading comprehension and controlled timed writing.

prerequisites.note: English 30-2 at 65% is another catalogue entry route.

courses.assessment: Timed proctored assessments during units. NO separate school final exam in the current VVS catalogue. BOTH Part A and Part B of the provincial English 30-1 diploma exam are required.
access_steps: Follow Moodle's unit assessment instructions and due dates.
Register separately for the diploma session in myPass.
Read the current VVS writing-centre and device instructions.
study_steps: Know your selected literary texts well enough to support an argument.
Read official writing exemplars and the student guide.
Practise permitted personal and critical responses, then check focus, evidence and conventions.
warnings: The generic school-exams page's all-30-level-final claim does not override this catalogue exception.
Waterloo uses the final blended English mark, not simply the higher school mark.
Check the enrolled course's current integrity rules before seeking any outside help.

courses.name: Social Studies 10-1
courses.subject: Social Studies
courses.purpose: Begin the Social Studies ladder used in the illustrated diploma route.
learn: Globalization and identity.
Effects on land, cultures, economies, human rights and quality of life.
Compare perspectives and support a position with sources.

prerequisites.note: Social Studies 10-2 at 65% is another entry route.

courses.assessment: Several timed Proctorio-supervised assessments, including a final exam. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Read Moodle's introduction and assessment release conditions.
Prepare webcam, microphone and a clear desk or table.
Follow the teacher's actual deadlines.
study_steps: Put major developments in order when chronology matters.
For each example, record whose perspective it represents.
Practise explaining both the benefit and cost of a policy or event.
warnings: Supervised assessments cannot be written on a bed.
Do not assume online means freely skippable coursework.

courses.name: Social Studies 20-1
courses.subject: Social Studies
courses.purpose: Continue toward Social Studies 30-1.
learn: Origins and forms of nationalism.
Nationalism in Canadian and international contexts.
Effects on citizenship, identity and international relations.

prerequisites.note: The course catalogue lists 60% in Social 10-1 or 20-2. The inspected prerequisite chart showed 65% for the 10-1 to 20-1 arrow. Confirm the discrepancy with VVS before registration; aiming at least 65% avoids relying on the lower entry threshold.

courses.assessment: Eight units and several timed Proctorio assessments, including a final exam. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Check the actual Moodle timeline.
Meet assessment release conditions before the closing dates.
Use a clear desk, webcam and microphone for supervised assessments.
study_steps: Distinguish national interest from nationalism.
Compare different interpretations of the same event.
Use precise examples rather than memorizing labels alone.
warnings: Prerequisite source discrepancy remains a registration check, not a resolved exemption.
The course is paced; being asynchronous does not remove deadlines.

courses.name: Social Studies 30-1
courses.subject: Social Studies
courses.purpose: Meet the Social Studies diploma category and add an academic senior subject.
learn: Ideology and identity.
Liberalism, individual and collective rights.
Democratic citizenship and evaluating competing positions.

prerequisites.note: Social 30-2 at 60% is another entry route.

courses.assessment: Timed supervised assessments, supervised midterm and final, plus the provincial diploma exam. Diploma registration is the student's separate responsibility.
access_steps: Order the required hard-copy Perspectives on Ideology textbook.
Read Moodle's paced unit timeline and exam conditions.
Register for the diploma session through myPass.
study_steps: Build your own ideology comparison chart.
Explain an argument with accurate historical or contemporary evidence.
Study official diploma response examples and scoring guidance under the course's permitted rules.
warnings: The catalogue explicitly treats AI use as plagiarism. Do not generate, rewrite or humanize course work with AI.
Assessments close at their due dates.
An online textbook is not an accepted replacement for the required hard copy.

courses.name: Mathematics 10C
courses.subject: Math
courses.purpose: Open the academic Math 20-1 and 30-1 ladder.
learn: Measurement, surface area and volume.
Trigonometry, exponents and radicals.
Relations, functions, linear graphs and systems of equations.

prerequisites.note: The catalogue lists other transfer entries; this illustration uses the Grade 9 route.

courses.assessment: Eight units; four supervised tests and a supervised final. The final is required for credit. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Read the Moodle timeline and release conditions.
Prepare the approved calculator and required external webcam.
Use practice quizzes before requesting or opening the permitted supervised test.
study_steps: Solve without copying an example's steps.
Keep an error log separating algebra, concept and calculator mistakes.
Retest mixed problems after correcting a weakness.
warnings: Intentional pacing still applies.
Use only tools allowed in the actual assessment.

courses.name: Mathematics 20-1
courses.subject: Math
courses.purpose: Prepare for Math 30-1 and calculus-intensive university study.
learn: Quadratic functions and equations.
Radicals, trigonometry, sequences and series.
Rational expressions, absolute-value and reciprocal functions, equations and inequalities.

prerequisites.note: Math 20-2 at 70% or Math 30-2 at 60% are alternate catalogue entries.

courses.assessment: Seven units; four supervised tests and a supervised final required for credit. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Follow the enrolled timeline.
Prepare the approved graphing calculator and external webcam.
Meet each test's release conditions.
study_steps: Explain why a transformation changes a graph.
Practise algebra separately from calculator work.
Mix old and new problem types instead of repeating one pattern.
warnings: A passing credit mark need not satisfy Math 30-1 entry.
Assessment timing is controlled by the course, not by this planning guide.

courses.name: Mathematics 30-1
courses.subject: Math
courses.purpose: Meet a common CS prerequisite and prepare for Math 31.
learn: Trigonometry and transformations.
Logarithms and operations on functions.
Permutations, combinations and the binomial theorem.

prerequisites.note: Math 30-2 at 75% is an alternate catalogue entry.

courses.assessment: Six units; four supervised tests, a supervised school final and a separate provincial diploma exam. Both school and diploma marks are needed for the normal official transcript mark.
access_steps: Complete Moodle's required work and supervised tests.
Use the approved calculator and camera arrangement.
Register separately in myPass for the diploma exam.
study_steps: Use official practice items after learning each topic.
Show the reasoning, not only a final answer.
Check calculator restrictions and practise with the permitted tools.
warnings: The school final and provincial diploma are different assessments.
Exam session dates cannot be moved just by studying faster.

courses.name: Mathematics 31
courses.subject: Math
courses.purpose: Learn calculus and meet the checked Waterloo CS prerequisite and Toronto calculus equivalent.
learn: Precalculus, limits and derivatives.
Derivative applications and curve sketching.
Trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions, and integrals.

prerequisites.note: The catalogue allows Math 30-1 at the same time, or after completing it with at least 50%. School load approval is separate.

courses.assessment: Seven units; four supervised tests and a supervised final required for credit. NO provincial diploma exam. The course is non-calculator-based.
access_steps: Open the Moodle introduction after approved registration.
Prepare the external webcam view of hands, papers and upper body.
Follow test and final release conditions.
study_steps: Explain a derivative as a rate of change.
Practise symbolic work without a calculator.
Connect a formula, graph and real situation.
warnings: The generic all-30-level-diploma statement does not apply.
Concurrent eligibility does not mean the combined workload is automatically manageable.

courses.name: Science 10
courses.subject: Science
courses.purpose: Open the Physics and Chemistry 20 ladders.
learn: Foundations of biology.
Foundations of chemistry and physics.
Earth science and using evidence across scientific disciplines.

prerequisites.note: Science 14 at 65% or Science 24 at 60% are alternate catalogue entries.

courses.assessment: Four unit exams and one final. Some are supervised with Proctorio. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Get the assigned textbook and science data booklet.
Read the Moodle exam requirements.
Prepare webcam and microphone for supervised assessments.
study_steps: Use diagrams and explain every arrow or label.
Distinguish an observation from an explanation.
Practise calculations with units and scientific interpretation.
warnings: This broad course does not remove the separate math prerequisite for Physics or Chemistry 20.

courses.name: Science 30
courses.subject: Science
courses.purpose: Complete the selected general-science route alongside Physics and Chemistry.
learn: Circulation and genetics.
Acid-base and organic chemistry.
Electromagnetic radiation and energy resources.

prerequisites.note: The catalogue also accepts Science 20 at 65%, but Science 20 is not selected. Physics 20 or Chemistry 20 at 65% is sufficient. Science 10 stays in this route for Physics 20 and Chemistry 20 prerequisites.

courses.assessment: Four supervised unit exams, a supervised midterm and final, plus the provincial diploma exam. Both course and diploma marks are required for the official final transcript mark.
access_steps: Obtain the Science 30 textbook and science data booklet.
Follow the enrolled Moodle timeline and exam release conditions.
Register separately for the diploma session in myPass.
study_steps: Connect each scientific model to evidence.
Practise calculations with units and explain diagrams.
Review the current diploma guide and permitted data booklet.
warnings: Registration depends on final prerequisite marks and school approval.
Science 30 includes biology topics even though separate Biology courses are not selected.

courses.name: Physics 20
courses.subject: Physics
courses.purpose: Build the route toward Physics 30 and a senior lab-science subject.
learn: Kinematics and dynamics.
Circular motion and gravitation.
Mechanical waves.

prerequisites.note: Both are required in the regular-term catalogue.

courses.assessment: Four supervised unit exams, a supervised midterm and final. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Obtain the required textbook and data booklet.
Read the course release conditions.
Prepare the approved supervised-assessment setup.
study_steps: Draw a labelled situation before calculating.
Choose equations from a physical explanation.
Check directions, units and whether the answer is plausible.
warnings: Summer and regular-term catalogues can have different wording. Use the correct session's rules.

courses.name: Physics 30
courses.subject: Physics
courses.purpose: Provide a senior academic science and additional 30-level diploma credits.
learn: Momentum and impulse.
Forces and fields.
Electromagnetic radiation and atomic physics.

prerequisites.note: A final prerequisite mark is required for normal registration.

courses.assessment: Supervised midterm and school final, plus the provincial diploma exam.
access_steps: Use the assigned textbook, workbook and Physics 30 data booklet.
Meet Moodle release conditions for school exams.
Register separately in myPass for the diploma exam.
study_steps: Sketch field and radiation diagrams carefully.
Practise explaining a model's limits.
Use official released items and the permitted data booklet.
warnings: Both school and diploma marks are normally needed for the official final mark.

courses.name: Chemistry 20
courses.subject: Chemistry
courses.purpose: Keep a second science discipline and satisfy routes that need Chemistry 20, including the checked UBC Vancouver Science preparation.
learn: Chemical bonding.
Solutions, acids and bases.
Quantitative relationships in chemical change.

prerequisites.note: Both are required by the regular-term catalogue used here. The summer catalogue has different entry wording and cannot be substituted silently.

courses.assessment: Supervised midterm and final in the regular-term catalogue. No provincial diploma exam.
access_steps: Get the assigned textbook and chemistry data booklet.
Read the current course timeline.
Follow Moodle's supervised-exam instructions.
study_steps: Connect a particle diagram to an equation.
Balance and interpret reactions before calculating.
Check units and explain what the result means.
warnings: Use the actual regular-term or summer prerequisite rules for the enrolled session.
Chemistry 30 is selected next, with a 65% Chemistry 20 prerequisite.

courses.name: Chemistry 30
courses.subject: Chemistry
courses.purpose: Complete the selected Chemistry ladder and add a senior academic science.
learn: Thermochemistry and the heat of a reaction.
Electrochemistry and batteries.
Organic chemistry, fossil-fuel reactions and acid-base equilibrium.

prerequisites.note: Chemistry 20 must be completed with at least 65% before normal entry.

courses.assessment: Four supervised unit tests and a supervised school final, plus the provincial diploma exam. Both course and diploma marks are required for the official final transcript mark.
access_steps: Obtain the Chemistry Alberta 20-30 textbook and chemistry data booklet.
Follow the enrolled Moodle timeline and supervised-test instructions.
Register separately for the diploma session in myPass.
study_steps: Explain energy changes before calculating.
Connect chemical equations with particle models.
Practise equilibrium and electrochemistry using permitted resources.
warnings: A passing Chemistry 20 credit alone may not meet the 65% entry threshold.
The school final and diploma exam are separate assessments.

courses.name: French 10-3Y
courses.subject: French
courses.purpose: Begin the selected French 10-3Y, 20-3Y and 30-3Y sequence. University language equivalence still needs confirmation.
learn: Listening, speaking, reading and writing in beginner French.
Complete everyday sentences about school, family and free time.

prerequisites.note: English 10-2 at 65% is another entry. No previous French is necessary. The first-fall illustration relies on FINAL Grade 9 LA, not concurrent English 10.

courses.assessment: Moodle and Vista Higher Learning lessons, written/spoken assessments, supervised midterm and final. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Open Moodle and the assigned VHL access after registration.
Follow the speaking and written task instructions.
Meet supervised-exam release conditions.
study_steps: Say and write small original sentences.
Practise listening before reading a transcript.
Review vocabulary in short repeated sessions.
warnings: Placement at a higher level requires a school placement exercise.
Five Alberta credits do not automatically establish a UC subject-year equivalence.

courses.name: French 20-3Y
courses.subject: French
courses.purpose: Continue the selected French ladder toward French 30-3Y.
learn: Intermediate listening, speaking, reading and writing.
Aspects of the contemporary francophone world.

prerequisites.note: The school can assess prior language experience for placement. Summer entry needs a final eligible prerequisite before its deadline.

courses.assessment: Moodle/VHL lessons and written/spoken work, with a supervised midterm and final. No diploma exam.
access_steps: Use the school's Moodle and VHL instructions.
Check the correct summer or regular-term timeline.
Prepare for supervised assessments.
study_steps: Use earlier vocabulary in new contexts.
Speak without reading a prepared translation.
Review errors in grammar and comprehension.
warnings: Two course levels are not yet a confirmed US two-year-language mapping.
Future summer availability is unconfirmed.

courses.name: French 30-3Y
courses.subject: French
courses.purpose: Complete the selected three-year French as a Second Language sequence.
learn: Advanced everyday listening, speaking, reading and writing.
Employment, the environment and technology.
More detailed study of the contemporary francophone world.

prerequisites.note: French 20 at 65% is the normal entry. Prior language experience can be assessed through a school placement exercise.

courses.assessment: Moodle and Vista Higher Learning lessons with written or spoken assessments, a supervised midterm and final. No provincial diploma exam.
access_steps: Use the assigned Moodle and Vista Higher Learning access after approved registration.
Follow the course speaking and writing instructions.
Meet release conditions for the supervised midterm and final.
study_steps: Listen and respond without reading a prepared translation.
Write original sentences about familiar topics.
Review recurring grammar and comprehension errors.
warnings: French as a Second Language 30-3Y is not French Language Arts 30-1 or Francais 30-1.
Alberta course levels do not by themselves prove UC language-year equivalence.

courses.name: Physical Education 10, three-credit version
courses.subject: Options
courses.purpose: Meet the minimum PE 10 diploma requirement.
learn: Active living across alternate environments, dance, flexibility/gymnastics, games and individual activities.
Reflect on activity, nutrition and health.

prerequisites.note: No prerequisite listed.

courses.assessment: 50 actual hours of activity across all five dimensions, minimum five hours in each, seven projects and supervisor declarations. All activities must be supervised by someone over 18; parents may supervise.
access_steps: Read the current Moodle activity and declaration requirements.
Arrange a genuine adult supervisor before logging activities.
Complete the projects and submit real records through the approved course.
study_steps: Plan varied activities that fit the five dimensions.
Record actual activity promptly.
Complete each reflection from what you did.
warnings: Never invent hours, activities or supervisor declarations.
This course cannot be compressed below its real activity requirements merely by writing faster.

courses.name: Career and Life Management
courses.subject: Options
courses.purpose: Meet the CALM diploma requirement and develop everyday decision skills.
learn: Personal development and healthy choices.
Well-informed decisions about life and future plans.

prerequisites.note: No course prerequisite listed. Junior-high credit restrictions and transition-summer rules are separate.

courses.assessment: The catalogue says there are NO supervised exams. Required course work still applies.
access_steps: Register only through the approved school program.
Read the Moodle introduction and required work.
Use the parent/guardian permission process for optional Human Sexuality content when applicable.
study_steps: Connect choices to real situations.
Complete the assigned work yourself.
Check that the final credit award is recorded.
warnings: Human Sexuality is an optional component with parent/guardian approval for students under 18.
No supervised exam does not mean no assignments.

courses.name: COM1255: E-Learning and Learning Management Systems
courses.subject: Options
courses.purpose: Complete the VVS introduction if it has not already been completed; count its one credit once.
learn: Using Moodle and learning-management systems.
Online ethics and digital literacy.

prerequisites.note: VVS must confirm term placement and whether a prior credit award already exists.

courses.assessment: Complete the actual module assessments and requirements in the enrolled Moodle course. This is one credit, not an unnamed multi-credit CTS group.
access_steps: Confirm with VVS whether COM1255 was previously completed.
If not completed, take the mandatory introduction in the term VVS specifies.
Verify its single credit award without counting it twice.
study_steps: Practise using the actual course navigation and submission tools.
Follow the module instructions and online conduct rules.
warnings: Mandatory if not previously completed.
If already awarded, keep that existing one credit in the total and do not retake or duplicate it.
Term placement is VVS-confirmed, not promised in a summer session.
CTS credit is not a Waterloo or Toronto academic admission subject.

exams.name: VVS course tests and finals
required_for: Assessments specified by the enrolled course outline
exams.purpose: Show that you understand the course outcomes. They contribute to the school-awarded mark.
learn: The specific unit outcomes or cumulative course content named in the outline.
How to explain reasoning, solve unfamiliar problems and use only permitted resources.
exams.format: Usually Moodle with Proctorio for supervised online tests. Teacher-approved campus or external supervision may be available. Exact duration, tools and weighting are course-specific.
access_steps: Sign in to your private Moodle account and open the enrolled course.
Read the introduction, timeline and release conditions. Finish the required preceding work.
Prepare valid photo ID, cameras/microphone and the permitted workspace/tools. Course-specific camera rules may be stricter than the general page.
Use the released assessment link only when ready. Do not start a timed attempt just to inspect it.
For campus supervision, obtain teacher permission and book through VVS with 2-3 school days' notice. The published regular slots are 9:00 and 12:00; confirm the actual booking.
An external supervisor requires school approval and their application at least five days before the exam. They cannot be a friend or relative.
prepare_steps: Make a list of outcomes from the outline.
Try permitted practice without notes to find weak spots.
Correct and retest the weak spots.
Check the setup before the actual assessment, using a practice/system-check route.
Plan enough time for the whole sitting; follow the teacher's accommodation process.
warnings: A visible link does not prove an assessment is unlocked or unfinished.
Summer supervised assessments require Proctorio under the published VVS rule.
Do not bypass room scans, monitoring or release conditions.
English 30-1 has no separate school final; Math 31 has a final but no diploma. Follow subject-specific rules.
School supervision software is not the Vretta writing-centre setup used for diploma exams.

exams.name: Grade 9 Provincial Achievement Tests
required_for: The Grade 9 provincial assessment program, subject to school/provincial exemptions
exams.purpose: Measure Grade 9 achievement across English, math, science and Social Studies. These are not university entrance exams and do not award high-school credits.
learn: The Grade 9 outcomes in each of the four core subjects.
English writing and reading, math reasoning and computation, scientific interpretation and Social Studies source interpretation.
Use the actual course outline and provincial practice material for the detailed topic list.
exams.format: VVS describes online PATs at supervised writing sessions. English and math have separate parts. Online does not mean an unsupervised home sitting.
access_steps: Look for the school's registration email and current PAT instructions.
Register for the actual school writing session using the school-provided process.
Confirm the specific date, location and device arrangement.
Prepare the approved personal device in advance or arrange the school Chromebook.
If the location is an extensive distance away, ask VVS about an approved local-school arrangement. It is not guaranteed.
Use the public Vretta practice area for familiarization, not a protected exam code.
prepare_steps: Review the course outcomes and your own error log.
Practise each part separately, then a realistic mixed set.
Use official sample questions and platform practice.
Check the current student instructions for permitted tools and timing.
warnings: The saved VVS PAT page still displayed 2025-26 dates. Those dates are NOT a 2026-27 schedule.
January 2026 provincial cancellations are a historical exception, not a current exemption.
Do not assume PAT registration happens through the diploma myPass process.
The guide does not claim that a particular student is registered or must write every sitting.

exams.name: Alberta diploma exams
required_for: Normal final transcript marks in designated diploma-exam courses
exams.purpose: Provide the provincial portion of a senior course's official final mark. The normal blend is 70% school mark and 30% diploma mark.
learn: The outcomes of the particular senior course.
The exam's response formats and scoring standards from its current student guide.
For this selected route: English 30-1, Social Studies 30-1, Math 30-1, Physics 30, Chemistry 30 and Science 30. Math 31 and French 30-3Y have no provincial diploma exam.
exams.format: At VVS, digitally accessed in Vretta while supervised IN PERSON at the assigned writing centre. English and Social Studies have Part A and Part B. Not all senior courses or exam sessions use the same structure.
access_steps: Check the correct academic-year significant dates and available session for your course.
Sign in privately to myPass and register for the course/session before the deadline. Course registration does not automatically register the exam.
Use the designated VVS South or North writing centre under current school instructions, not a provincial centre by assumption.
Read the school confirmation for the actual venue. Do not assume the Calgary campus is the venue.

Prepare the required Respondus LockDown Browser/device setup in advance. VVS's current diploma page permits a personal laptop/MacBook or arranged school Chromebook, not a personal Chromebook, phone or iPad.
Bring accepted photo ID and permitted equipment. VVS recommends arrival at 8:30 for a 9:00 exam or 12:30 for a 13:00 exam.
At the venue, connect to Wi-Fi, sign into Vretta and use the unique exam code supplied by the supervisor.
Check myPass for results about three weeks after writing. A results statement is not the official transcript.
prepare_steps: Read the current course-specific guide and information bulletin.
Review released questions or student-writing exemplars.

A provincial achievement test at specified school grades. It is not a university entrance test.
A course assessment set by the school. It is separate from a provincial diploma exam.

VVS's learning platform for courses, activities, assignments and many school assessments.

Career and Technology Studies modules. Many award one credit. Count distinct actual awards, not a guessed bundle.
A requirement that must be satisfied before a course activity or assessment becomes available.
UC's seven subject groups totalling 15 subject years. Alberta credit totals do not automatically prove these equivalences.
An eligibility floor. Meeting it does not guarantee competitive admission.
An offer that still requires stated marks, course completion or documents.
Waterloo's Admission Information Form, required for the checked CS application.
A program combining study with approved work terms. Employment and earnings are not guaranteed.
A field selected within a degree. Some routes, such as UBC Vancouver Science to CS, have a second selection step.
A policy under which a request for aid can affect admission selection.
The amount of financial need determined by the university's process, not simply the amount a family asks for.
Published cost before any aid. It may cover only an academic year rather than all twelve months.
Permission to begin an offered place later. University-specific conditions apply.
A school-issued US student document. It is not immigration status or work authorization on its own.
